WebRoot/auth/admin/addER.jsp: As a user within a healthcare administrative system, you have the capability to add new Emergency Responders to the system. To do this, you will need to enter the necessary details such as the first name, last name, and a valid email address of the Emergency Responder in question. In cases where an email address is unavailable, the hospital's predefined email address should be used for password recovery purposes. Once the form is completed, the system will process the information and generate a new unique ID and a temporary password for the Emergency Responder. You will be informed of these details on the confirmation screen, where you are encouraged to relay this information to the new Emergency Responder to facilitate their access to the system. This process streamlines the onboarding of Emergency Responders to ensure that they are duly registered and have secure access credentials to perform their duties.

WebRoot/auth/admin/addHCP.jsp: This interface allows authorized administrative personnel to add new healthcare providers into the system. As an administrative user, you can input the first name, last name, and email address of the new healthcare provider. If the new provider does not have a personal email, you should use a designated email address for password recovery purposes. Upon submission, the system will create a new account for the provider, assigning them a medical identification number and a temporary password. You will see a confirmation message with the new provider's details, which you need to communicate to the provider. If any errors are encountered during form submission, such as validation issues, they will be displayed for correction. After successfully adding the new provider, you can proceed to update their details if necessary.

WebRoot/auth/admin/addPHA.jsp:
As a user interacting with this system, you have the ability to add a new Public Health Authority (PHA) to the organizational records. Begin by ensuring you have the new personnel's first name, last name, and a valid email address ready. If the individual lacks a personal email address, use the organization-provided email address. Fill out this information in the respective fields provided in the form on the page. Upon completing the form, submit it to register the new PHA.

Once the form is submitted, the system will process the details and create a new personnel entry. If successful, the page will display a confirmation message along with the new Medical ID (MID) assigned to the PHA, as well as a temporary password. Ensure this information is securely delivered to the new personnel for their records and access. In the event of any errors during this process, such as invalid form entries, the system will display an error message indicating the issue.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editApptType.jsp: As an administrative user managing appointment types, you can customize the categories of appointments within your system. On the page, you will find a form to either add new appointment types or update existing ones. To create a new type, input the desired name and duration, then submit the form by clicking "Add Type." For updates, you can click on an existing appointment type from the list displayed, which will autofill the form with the selected details. After making any necessary changes, click "Update Type" to save your modifications. The system also provides feedback through messages to guide you in correcting any input errors.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editCPTProcedureCodes: This system allows healthcare administrators to manage a list of Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes used in medical billing and records. As a user, you can view existing procedure codes and their descriptions, identify whether they are related to immunizations, and update or add new procedure codes through a form. The interactions include inputting or selecting a procedure code and description, marking if it's for immunization by checking a box, and submitting the form to add or update the details. If you encounter any errors with the entered data, informative messages will guide you to correct them. This promotes accurate and updated maintenance of medical procedures within the system, critical for efficient healthcare administration.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editICDCodes.jsp: Users of this system can manage healthcare-related codes called ICD codes, which are essential for classifying diagnoses. The process is initiated by logging into a secure environment, where users can view the current list of ICD codes displaying their details, such as code number, description, and classification. Users interact primarily through a form interface that allows them to add new ICD codes or update existing ones. When adding or updating a code, users need to input a code number, specify if it is a chronic condition by ticking a checkbox, and provide a detailed description. Once submitted, the system processes this information and updates accordingly. Error messages guide users by indicating if any input validation issues occur, ensuring only accurate and complete data entries are accepted. This process helps maintain an accurate and up-to-date database of ICD codes crucial for consistent diagnosis classification within the healthcare facility.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editLOINCCodes.jsp:
This system facilitates the maintenance of LOINC (Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes) codes, which are used for identifying health measurements, observations, and documents. As a user interacting with this interface, you can perform several key functions:

1. **Viewing LOINC Codes**: Upon accessing the page, you will be presented with a list of current LOINC codes displayed in a tabulated format. Each code is accompanied by its associated properties such as Component, Kind of Property, Time Aspect, System, Scale Type, and Method Type.

2. **Updating LOINC Codes**: You can select any existing LOINC code from the list to update. By clicking on a specific attribute of a LOINC code (like Code, Component, etc.), its value will populate the corresponding field in the form located above the table. You are advised to fill in all fields with the original information if you do not wish to modify them. Once you have made the necessary changes, submit the update to apply it.

3. **Adding New LOINC Codes**: The form also allows you to add a new LOINC code. You need to fill out all fields within the form specifying the details for the new entry and then submit it to be added to the list of LOINC codes.

For both adding or updating codes, a submission will trigger the system’s validation rules, and you will be informed of any issues through a message. The interface will use colors to signal the success or failure of your action; a red background for errors or a green background for successful operations.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editNDCInteractions.j: The system enables healthcare or pharmacy users, typically in an administrative role, to record and manage interactions between different National Drug Codes (NDC). The user interface provides dropdown menus for selecting two distinct drug codes from a list. Users are required to enter a description of the interaction, which could detail potential adverse effects when the drugs are used together. Once the necessary information is inputted, the user can submit this data by clicking an "Add Interaction" button. The system will then process this information, attempting to record the interaction, and provide feedback on the operation's success or any errors encountered. These functions aid healthcare providers in maintaining comprehensive records of drug interactions, potentially improving patient safety and care outcomes by preventing harmful drug combinations. If users wish to return to editing drug codes, there is an option to navigate back to a previous page dedicated to that purpose.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editNDCodes.jsp:
As a user of this system, you have the capability to manage National Drug Codes (NDC), which are identifiers for medications. This tool allows you to perform several key functions to maintain and update these codes within the system. You can view a list of current medications along with their unique NDCs and descriptions. If you want to add new medication codes, you can input the code and description, and click "Add Code" to register it in the system. Additionally, you can update existing codes by selecting an entry from the list, modifying the details, and clicking "Update Code" to save changes.

The tool also provides functionality to manage drug interaction information. If there are any interactions associated with a specific NDC, you can review the other drugs involved in these interactions. You have the option to delete a specific interaction by selecting it and confirming the deletion. The system ensures that any operation involving adding, updating, or deleting codes or interactions requires validation to prevent errors, and provides feedback for successful operations or issues encountered during the process.

Overall, this tool is designed to streamline the process of maintaining an accurate and updated list of drug codes and interactions, ensuring safety and compliance in medication management.

WebRoot/auth/admin/home.jsp: As a user, when you access the platform with administrative privileges, you will be greeted with a personalized welcome message on the main page. This message will include your name, providing a user-friendly and personalized experience each time you log in. You can expect a consistent page structure with a recognizable header and footer, ensuring easy navigation and a familiar interface as you manage your administrative tasks.

WebRoot/auth/admin/hospitalAssignments.j:
As a user responsible for managing staff assignments within a hospital system, you will access a page dedicated to handling the assignments of healthcare professionals to different hospitals. Upon loading this page, the system first checks for your personnel ID to ensure you have the necessary permissions to make changes. If the ID is not present, you are redirected to obtain it.

Once you have access, the system displays two tables. The first table lists hospitals to which healthcare professionals are currently assigned, where you can unassign a professional from a hospital by clicking the provided link. The second table shows hospitals that are available for new assignments, allowing you to assign healthcare professionals to hospitals by clicking the respective link.

This functionality supports efficient management of hospital staffing, ensuring professionals are assigned to appropriate locations as needed.

WebRoot/auth/admin/hospitalListing.jsp:
In this system, the purpose is to facilitate interactions with a hospital listing and assignment management interface. Users, typically administrators, can manage hospital records by adding new hospitals or updating existing ones. 

Upon accessing the page, you will see a current list of hospitals along with fields to input a hospital ID and name. You can add a new hospital by filling in these fields and clicking "Add Hospital." If you wish to update an existing hospital's information, click on the hospital name in the list, which will populate the fields for editing. After making changes, click "Update Hospital Information" to save changes. The system provides feedback such as error messages if validation fails during data entry, ensuring only accurate and complete data is submitted.

WebRoot/auth/admin/information.jsp: The system is designed to present personnel information for an administrative user in a healthcare application. When you, as an administrator, log into the system, you will see a profile page showcasing specific details about the personnel. You'll be greeted with a profile picture followed by their name and a placeholder location. The interface is simplified, focusing only on key identity information. Through this setup, you can quickly ascertain basic details of healthcare personnel, aiding in efficient personnel management and oversight within the healthcare network.

WebRoot/auth/admin/menu.jsp: In this system, as an admin user, you can perform several key operations to manage healthcare roles and system settings. To start, you have the option to add new healthcare roles such as healthcare providers, emergency responders, and public health administrators. If you need to make modifications, you can edit various settings including appointment types, hospital assignments for healthcare providers, and different medical codes, which are integral to healthcare processes. These codes include procedure codes, drug codes, diagnosis codes, and laboratory codes. Additionally, you have the ability to update personnel records and manage your own demographic information. The system also facilitates sending appointment reminders and tracking these through an outbox. Other administrative functions include managing hospital listings, configuring session timeout settings, and reviewing satisfaction survey results to improve service quality. These activities ensure the healthcare facility's operations are efficiently managed and aligned with users' needs and expectations.

WebRoot/auth/admin/remindersMessageOutbo: As a user of this system, you access the Reminders Message Outbox to review messages that need your attention. These messages are sorted and displayed based on criteria that you can set. You have the ability to sort messages by the name of the recipient or by the date they were sent. Additionally, you can choose to view these sorted lists either in ascending or descending order. Each message is displayed with information like the recipient, subject, and the date it was sent. Unread messages are highlighted to easily catch your attention. If a message piques your interest, you can click on it to read its details. If there are no messages at the moment, the system will inform you accordingly. This interaction ensures efficient management and tracking of your outgoing reminders, essential for maintaining timely communication and effective message handling.

WebRoot/auth/admin/sendAppointmentRemind: As an administrative user within a healthcare system, you can send appointment reminders to patients by accessing the send appointment reminders interface. Start by entering the number of days in advance you'd like to remind patients about their upcoming appointments. This value will determine how far into the future appointments are considered for reminders. Once entered, submit the form to initiate the sending process. The system reviews upcoming appointments within the specified period, prepares messages containing the appointment details and sends them to patients, ensuring they are reminded in a timely manner. After processing, a confirmation is shown indicating the number of reminders successfully dispatched.

WebRoot/auth/admin/sessionTimeout.jsp: As a user of this system, you can adjust the duration of time before your session automatically ends due to inactivity. To change the session timeout settings, you will see a prompt to enter the desired number of minutes you would like your account to remain active before requiring re-authentication. Ensure that you input a minimum of one minute. Once you submit your desired timeout duration, the change will be noted, although it will only take effect the next time you log in. A confirmation message will indicate that the session timeout has been updated.

WebRoot/auth/admin/viewAllReportRequests:
As a user, you can manage report requests within the healthcare administration system. Here’s how you interact with the system:

1. View All Report Requests: You can see a list of all the report requests. This includes details such as the ID, patient information, approver details, dates for request, approval, and viewing, the current status of the report request, and any comments associated with it.

2. Approve Requests: If a report request is still pending, you, as an authorized user, can approve it. Simply click on the “Approve” link next to the request you wish to approve. Confirmation of the approval will be displayed on the screen.

3. Reject Requests: If you decide to reject a report request, click on the “Reject” link. You will be prompted to provide a reason for the rejection. Enter the details and confirm. A confirmation of the rejection will be displayed.

4. Error Handling: In case of any issues during approval or rejection, an error message will be displayed to alert you of what went wrong.

This system streamlines the approval process of healthcare report requests, ensuring efficient administration within the healthcare environment.

WebRoot/auth/admin/viewReminderMessage.j:
This application is designed for users to access and view reminder messages. When a user wishes to view the details of a specific reminder message, they navigate to a message interface where the message list is preloaded. The user selects a particular message from this list by clicking it.

Upon selection, the application fetches the message details, including the recipient, subject, date, time, and content of the message. The chosen message is then marked as read to update its status and is stored for session continuity. If any issues arise, like incorrect input or session data absence, the user is redirected accordingly to ensure they remain engaged in the system's messaging workflow. This functionality commonly supports healthcare management systems by providing accurate and timely communication between practitioners and patients or within administrative layers.

WebRoot/auth/admin/visitGraph.jsp:
As a user of the healthcare visit trend analysis system, you can generate reports to understand patient visit trends over a specified period. You can begin by selecting a starting and an ending month and year from the available dropdown options, which will allow you to define the timeframe of interest for your report. After setting your desired timeframe, you simply click the button to generate the report, which will analyze patient visit data and present you with a visual representation.

The system provides a detailed graph illustrating the number of visits by minors and adults for each month within your selected period. It ensures accuracy by preventing users from selecting an invalid timeframe where the start date is after the end date or the end date is in the future.

When generating the report, if data is available, the result will showcase the number of visits, with the graph depicting both categories (minors and adults) using distinct colors. This visual aid allows you to quickly assess visit patterns and any discernible trends over the months you have selected.

If any errors occur, such as selecting a timeframe that is not permissible, the system will alert you with an error message, preventing further actions until corrections are made.

Overall, this tool assists healthcare administrators in understanding patient flow and trends, thereby optimizing scheduling and resource allocation.

WebRoot/auth/er/home.jsp: As a user of this system, when you access the home section specifically tailored for the emergency room (ER) personnel, you will be greeted with the latest updates and notifications relevant to your role. The page features a straightforward list of announcements highlighting new functionalities that aim to enhance your workflow efficiency. For example, an intuitive calendar pop-up feature has been implemented, allowing you to select dates quickly without manual entry, reducing potential input errors. The notifications section is designed to keep you informed about important updates or alerts that require your attention during your shift. This streamlined interface is crafted to ensure you have access to the necessary resources and updates pertinent to your responsibilities in providing timely care in the medical facility.

WebRoot/auth/er/information.jsp: As a user interacting with this system, you would be able to view personal information for a specific medical personnel member. Upon accessing this feature, you would see an image associated with the individual's unique identifier, followed by their full name and location details, including the city and state where they reside. This information is important in a healthcare setting for confirming identity and ensuring you are viewing the correct personnel's details.

WebRoot/auth/er/menu.jsp: As a user interacting with this system, you will navigate within a digital platform aimed at managing healthcare-related tasks. You will see a section dedicated to reports, where you can access different types of patient information. Specifically, through this section, you can generate or view an emergency patient report. This feature is likely to be used when quick and accessible patient data is required, particularly in urgent medical situations where immediate access to a patient's health record is critical. This ensures healthcare professionals have the necessary information at their fingertips to make informed decisions in emergency scenarios.

WebRoot/auth/exceptionHandler.jsp: Users interacting with this system encounter a mechanism that gracefully handles unexpected issues by capturing details about them. When an issue arises, the system gathers the essential details and presents a user-friendly error message instead of a technical error. This ensures that the user experience is smooth and informed. Following this, the user is directed to a specific page designed to guide them through resolving the issue or understanding more about it. This approach ensures users are not left confused and can continue their interactions with minimal disruption. The system aims to maintain operational continuity by efficiently managing errors behind the scenes and providing clear communication to the user.

WebRoot/auth/forwardUser.jsp: As a user, upon authentication, you are forwarded to your specific homepage based on your role in the system. If identified as a patient, you are directed to the patient homepage, where you can manage your health information. As a healthcare provider, you are taken to the healthcare provider interface to access patient data and treatment options. Administrative and emergency roles are channeled to their respective sections, allowing access to system management or emergency services. Unauthorized access leads to an error page or redirects to the system's main entry if your session is invalid.

WebRoot/auth/getPatientID.jsp:
As a user looking to select a patient from a healthcare management system, this feature facilitates the search and selection process of a patient's identifier. Upon reaching this segment of the system, you will encounter options to search for a patient by entering their first and last name. Once you provide this information, the system will attempt to locate matching patient records.

The core functionality includes a patient search feature where you input the necessary details and submit your search request. If there are matching patients, the system displays a list, showing identifiers along with names. You can then select the desired patient from this list.

This capability simplifies locating patients by their personal details and allows seamless integration into subsequent actions you may need to perform, such as accessing patient records or scheduling appointments. It ensures that you can effectively pinpoint a patient when working within a larger healthcare administrative workflow.

WebRoot/auth/getPersonnelID.jsp: To select a personnel member, you will first land on a page with the title "Please Select a Personnel". Here, you have options to search by first and last names of the personnel. By entering the desired names in the corresponding fields and submitting the search form, the system will search for personnel records matching the provided criteria. Once the search is executed, a list of personnel matching your search criteria will be displayed, showing details such as their identification number, first name, and last name. For each personnel member listed, you can click a button associated with their ID to select them. Upon selecting a personnel member, the action redirects to a subsequent workflow or process determined by the system's forward dynamic. This functionality is primarily designed for scenarios requiring user selection, such as roles in healthcare administration where personnel management is essential.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/addUAP.jsp: As part of a healthcare management system, this interface allows an administrative user to add a new User Account Personnel (UAP). The process begins with the completion and submission of a form, where the user inputs essential information such as the first name, last name, and email address of the new personnel. Upon submission, the system automatically assigns a role to the new user and attempts to process this information, creating a unique account for the personnel. If successful, the system provides feedback including the new user's identification number and a temporary password, which can be relayed to the user. The system ensures that the input data adheres to validation rules, and in the event of an error, it informs the administrator of the issue encountered, offering an opportunity to rectify and resubmit the details. After successfully adding the personnel, the user can navigate to view and possibly edit additional personnel details.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/calendar.jsp: As a user of this appointment calendar system, you can view and manage appointments efficiently. Upon accessing the calendar interface, you will first see a display of the current month's appointments in a calendar format. You can navigate between months using "Last" and "Next" links provided, which allow you to explore past and future appointments. Each day on the calendar checks for any appointments scheduled and displays them accordingly. You will notice clear indicators for any dates with appointments and, if applicable, conflicts are highlighted. For further details, you can click on any appointment to read more specific information about it. Overall, this system aids in scheduling by providing a streamlined calendar view to track and explore your appointments over time.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/editPatientList.jsp: Healthcare professionals can use this interface to manage their list of monitored patients. Initially, the system ensures that a specific patient has been selected for modification by requiring a patient ID. If not, they are redirected to select a patient from another page. Once a patient is chosen, the user can see options to either add the patient to their monitoring list or remove them if they are already included. After an action of adding or removing a patient, the user's list is updated, and a confirmation message is displayed, such as "Patient [Name] Added" or "Patient [Name] Removed". If they wish to switch to a different patient, they can do so using the provided option. This functionality supports healthcare patient management by allowing easy updates to whom they are actively monitoring.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/editRepresentatives.jsp:
To use the system for managing patient representatives, follow these steps: 

1. Ensure you have a patient ID. If you access the page without a patient ID, you will be redirected to the proper page to input or retrieve it.

2. On the page, you can see a list of current representatives assigned to the patient. If no representatives are yet assigned, you will be informed that no representatives are specified.

3. To remove an existing representative, click on the 'Remove' link next to their name. This action will update the list to reflect the changes.

4. To add a new representative, you will use the 'Find User' button next to 'Patient' to search for and select a user to assign as a representative. Once selected, you will see their information in the specified area.

5. After choosing a new representative, submit the form using the 'Represent this patient' button to update the representative list for the patient.

6. If there are any errors in the process, such as entering invalid information or processing issues, you will receive a message indicating the specific error. Otherwise, confirmation messages for successful additions or removals will be displayed.

This system ensures secure and efficient management of representatives for patient records, maintaining a robust method for healthcare professionals to assign or reassign patient accountability effectively.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/hcpConsultation.jsp:
The consultation module is designed for healthcare providers to manage consultation referrals for patients. It allows logged-in healthcare professionals to perform four main functions: initiating a new consultation, viewing pending consultations, updating consultation details, and sending consultation requests. 

1. To initiate a new consultation, the user selects a patient under their care and another healthcare provider to refer the patient to. They can then provide consultation details which will be included in the request.

2. To view pending consultations, both outgoing and incoming consultations are displayed, showing details such as consultation status, involved patients, and healthcare providers. Users can select a specific consultation to view or update further.

3. Updating a consultation involves reviewing existing consultation details, editing the referral or consultation notes, and changing the status of the consultation. This feature provides the ability to manage ongoing consultations and ensure that appropriate actions are taken throughout the process.

4. Sending a consultation request involves confirming the selection of the patient, the receiving healthcare provider, and the detailed message before submitting the consultation referral.

These interactions streamline the referral process between healthcare practitioners, enhancing the efficiency of patient care coordination within the medical facility.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/home.jsp: As a healthcare professional using this system, you can interact with several features designed to streamline your workflow. On the home page, you will find announcements of new features, like a calendar popup for easier date entry. You will also have access to notifications about report history. If there are comprehensive report requests, you can view the status of each request. For lab procedures completed in the last month, you can check the details for specific patients, including the procedure and its results. If needed, a link is provided to view all lab procedures. This system helps manage and review recent activities efficiently, improving patient management and administrative tasks.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/information.jsp: As a user interacting with this system focused on healthcare personnel management, you would first see a personalized dashboard upon logging in. This dashboard displays specific details about you, such as your name and location, reinforcing a professional identity within the medical community. A particular feature includes a visual cue with your profile picture for easy recognition, enhancing personalized interaction. This system provides a straightforward means to verify and review personal information, ensuring accurate and accessible data for healthcare professionals' administrative processes. The setup enhances the user experience by offering visual and textual identification, pivotal in maintaining an organized and efficient digital workplace.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/LabProcHCP.jsp: As a user of this system, you can view and manage laboratory procedures for patients. Initially, ensure you have selected a patient to view their lab results. If you haven't, the system will prompt you to choose a patient. Once you've selected a patient, you will see a table displaying detailed lab procedures, including the patient’s name, lab code, rights, status, commentary, results, office visit ID, and the last updated date. You have several actions available: you can edit the office visit details, manage the privacy settings to allow or disallow viewing of the procedure, and update the procedure itself. The interface will inform you if there are no lab procedures available for the selected patient.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/menu.jsp: If you are using this system, you can manage various healthcare-related tasks through a menu with categorized options. In the 'Add' section, you can add new patients or administrative personnel. The 'Edit' category allows you to update basic health information, personal demographics, patient details, and patient representatives. You can also edit details of administrative personnel. Appointments can be managed by scheduling new ones or viewing existing ones under the 'Appointments' section. The 'Messaging' section lets you access your message inbox and outbox for communications. In the 'View' section, you can look at patient visit history, appointment calendars, lab procedures, and any report requests. You can generate emergency patient reports in the 'Report' category. 'Telemedicine' functionalities include managing patient lists and monitoring patients remotely. Lastly, other tasks such as consultations, evaluating chronic disease risks, documenting office visits, viewing email history, setting visit reminders, analyzing survey results, and assessing prescription renewal needs are available in the 'Other' category. This structure supports efficient management and operational oversight in a healthcare environment.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/messageInbox.jsp:
In this system, users have the capability to manage and interact with their personal messages. Upon accessing the "My Messages" section, users can view a list of messages sent to them. If desired, users can utilize sorting options to arrange these messages based on sender's name or the time the message was received, either in ascending or descending order.

Additionally, users have the option to filter their messages. This includes setting criteria for messages by specifying attributes such as the sender, subject, particular words that messages should or should not contain, and the date range of the messages. Users can edit these filter settings and either test how the filter would work on their current messages without committing, or save the filter for ongoing use.

If the user decides to edit a filter, they can input and modify details such as the sender's name, message subject, words to include or exclude, and start and end dates. After altering these filters, users can test their effectiveness or save the changes. The session adapts to these preferences, allowing a tailored message viewing experience based on the user-defined filters.

When a message is read, its display appearance reflects its read status to differentiate from unread messages. If a user has no messages, the system prominently indicates this status. This structure supports a user's need for efficient message management by providing both automated sorting and custom filters to suit individual preferences.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/messageOutbox.jsp: As a user engaging with this system, you can manage your sent messages effectively. Begin by navigating to the section labeled "My Sent Messages" where you will see a list of all messages you have sent. If you wish to compose a new message, you can easily do so by selecting the link to compose a message. Furthermore, you have the ability to sort your list of sent messages by recipient name or the time they were sent. This sorting feature allows you to choose whether you want them displayed in ascending or descending order. If there are any messages in your outbox, they will be presented in a structured table showing the recipient, subject, and date sent, with an option to read the full content of any message. If no messages exist in your outbox, you will see a simple note informing you that no messages are present. Through these intuitive features, you can maintain efficient management and review of your sent correspondence.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/monitorPatients.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you have the ability to monitor patients' remote health data effectively. After logging in, this feature allows you to view a structured list of patient information including their blood pressure readings, glucose levels, and the date of the health data report. Patients' health readings that fall outside of normal ranges are highlighted to capture your attention, helping you quickly identify potential concerns. You can explore additional patient details by selecting individual patient entries. This system ensures that you are well-equipped to provide timely and informed care to your patients by keeping patient data organized and accessible.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/reply.jsp:
As a user engaged in a healthcare communication platform, you have the ability to reply to messages sent by patients or healthcare professionals. Within this environment, after identifying a message you want to reply to, you can initiate a response by interacting with a dedicated reply page. Here is how you can engage with this feature:

1. When you opt to reply to a message, the system retrieves the original message details, including who sent it and the subject line.

2. You are presented with a form where you can craft your reply. The form automatically fills in the subject line, prepending "RE:" to the original subject for continuity and context.

3. You will write your response in a dedicated text area provided in the form.

4. Once you are satisfied with your reply, you submit the form. The system sends your message to the original sender and logs the correspondence by associating it with the initial message, ensuring conversation threads are maintained efficiently.

5. Upon sending the reply, you are redirected back to your inbox, where you can view other messages and continue managing your communications.

This system streamlines direct communication between healthcare providers and patients, ensuring timely and organized exchanges in a professional healthcare setting.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/scheduleAppt.jsp: To schedule an appointment, start by navigating to the appointment scheduling page. If prompted, verify the patient you are managing or select a different one through the provided link. Once confirmed, proceed to fill out the required information on the form. Select the type of appointment by choosing from the available options which detail duration. Pick a date by clicking the date selection button, followed by setting the appointment time using the dropdown menus for hours, minutes, and AM/PM distinction. You can optionally add comments about the appointment for additional context. After ensuring all details are correct, submit the form to finalize the scheduling of the appointment. Upon submission, if successful, you'll see a confirmation and be redirected to the homepage, optimizing the coordination and preparation for upcoming interactions.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/sendEmailNotification.j: As a user, the interface provides you the ability to easily send email notifications if you are a healthcare professional logged into the system. Once logged in, if you choose to send an email, you are directed to a straightforward form where you can draft and send an email to a chosen patient. First, review the recipient’s default email contents that include your details as the sender. You can then fill in or adjust the recipient's email, input a custom subject, and compose or edit the email body text. After completing the form, you can either send the email or reset the fields if needed. Upon sending, the system confirms successful delivery by presenting the sent email details, reassured by greyed-out recalled information. You are also given the option to return to the main home page. This process facilitates efficient communication between healthcare providers and patients, streamlined for quick and effective outreach.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/sendMessage.jsp: This system is designed to facilitate communication within a healthcare context by allowing healthcare professionals to send secure messages to their patients. As a user, if you are a healthcare provider logged into the system, you can send a message to a patient by either first selecting a patient or being redirected to a patient selection interface if no patient is currently selected. Once a patient is selected, you can compose a message by entering a subject and the message text in the provided form and then clicking the "Send" button to dispatch the message.
